newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Profit-taking in index puts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Profit-taking in index puts.

text.p: As U.S. stocks rebounded from Monday's steep decline, investors sold puts in major stock index options to take profits, options traders said.
Put premiums expanded sharply on yesterday's selloff but fell hard on the rebound Tuesday.
"Calls haven't moved too much, relatively speaking, but the puts have lost a lot of premium, which is to be expected," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in S&P 100 index .OEX options.
But he added that buying and selling in both puts and calls has been steady throughout the session.
By about 1100 CDT/1600 GMT, the OEX was up 4.64 at 861.44, off its 864.06 session high. It tumbled nearly 20 points Monday.
Among other indexes, the S&P 500 .SPX rose 4.66 to 883.28 and September S&P 500 futures added 10.55 to 892.30.
An SPX futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said some brokerage firms were selling September puts off the opening.
"They're selling the volatility in the puts," he said. "Yesterday it got pumped up because we broke."
Futures volume was fairly light on the way down on Monday, he added.
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange, volatility as measured by the Volatility Index .VIX, which is calculated off certain OEX contracts, was down 0.91, or about 3.75 percent, at 23.20.
The VIX rose 1.67, or nearly 7.5 percent, on Monday.
The trader at the Merc said one highlight Tuesday was a three-way trade in some December contracts.
A firm was selling the December 750/970 strangle (750 puts and 970 calls) and buying the December 840 puts.
Despite the penchant for put selling, a big buyer of puts in the SPX was seen, Callahan said.
SPX volume was led by the July 870 puts, which traded about 5,750 contracts. The option, which was down 4-3/8 at 11-1/2, had open interest of 12,920, including an addition of 5,333 Monday.
Overall volume in SPX options by 1100 CDT/1600 GMT leaned heavily toward puts. Put volume was 19,695 compared to call volume of 9,037.
In the OEX, puts and calls were about even. Put volume totalled 19,092 against call volume of 19,963.
